def add_months(day: str, n: int) -> str:
    from datetime import date, timedelta
    
    # Parse the input date
    year, month, day_of_month = map(int, day.split('-'))
    
    # Calculate the target month and year
    target_month = month + n
    target_year = year
    
    # Normalize month and year (handle overflow/underflow)
    while target_month > 12:
        target_month -= 12
        target_year += 1
    while target_month < 1:
        target_month += 12
        target_year -= 1
    
    # Determine the last day of the target month
    if target_month == 12:
        last_day_of_target_month = 31
    else:
        # Find last day by getting the first day of next month and subtracting 1 day
        first_of_next = date(target_year, target_month + 1, 1)
        last_day_of_target_month = (first_of_next - timedelta(days=1)).day
    
    # Determine the last day of the original month
    if month == 12:
        last_day_of_original_month = 31
    else:
        first_of_next_original = date(year, month + 1, 1)
        last_day_of_original_month = (first_of_next_original - timedelta(days=1)).day
    
    # Apply billing rule
    if day_of_month == last_day_of_original_month:
        # Original day is last day of month -> use last day of target month
        target_day = last_day_of_target_month
    else:
        # Keep the same day, or use last day if target month is too short
        target_day = min(day_of_month, last_day_of_target_month)
    
    # Format and return the result
    return f"{target_year:04d}-{target_month:02d}-{target_day:02d}"
